$comment: LEVEL 4 -- DILIM. Every line is the apo's: Lolo stopped at the water (Dagat's farewell),
so `speaker_default` is "apo" and every line says so as well.
She talks to herself, and what she says is what Lola taught her -- memories of
instructions, not observations (Kent's design, 'NO GUIDE'). An arrival line says what
Lola said about the thing in front of her; it never says what to draw.
⚠ NO LINE MAY NAME A DRAWABLE CLASS. Here the traps are horse (the tikbalang),
tree (the kapre's perch), sun (the morning), clock (the finale) and fan. The check is
word-boundary and case-insensitive, and run_level4_audit.gd runs it.
⚠ NOTHING STORY-SHAPED MID-ENCOUNTER. A lore line pauses the whole tree; once something
is hunting her, only `kind: hint` lines (the hint bar, which never stops play) are said.
The arrivals below are said on the way in, before anything has moved.
RESPAWN is a pool: LevelBase says one per knockout, in turn, through the hint bar.
WHAT IS NOT HERE YET: each later encounter's answered and after lines, the
finale's waves and the morning. They come with the encounters that say them -- an
unreachable line is an audit failure, not a placeholder.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Lola painted this one. She used to tell me what lived in these woods.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: The manananggal. The tikbalang. She'd name them one by one, so I'd know them if I ever met one.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I thought she was scaring me. She was teaching me.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Lolo stopped at the water. From here it is only me, and what she taught me.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Lola said the woods take people who stop paying attention.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Lola said the dark is only dark. It is what is in it you watch for.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Lola said when the lamp goes out, you go back to where it was last lit.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: No more ink. The next clearing will give it back.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: A mound on the path, with things left all round it. Lola said: when you pass a punso, you ask first. Tabi-tabi po.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Tabi-tabi po. Excuse me -- I only need to pass.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: My foot -- it is swelling. I stood on it. Lola said it wears off if I keep going.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Something stirred in the mound. Lola said they remember the ones who ask.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Over, and not a crumb of it touched. Lola would still have asked.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: A clearing. Lola said: wherever you can make a **light** of your own, stop, and fill the lamp before you go on.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: There. Warm. The lamp drinks it up, and the dark steps back a little.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: These tracks go backwards. Lola said the sigbin waits where it is darkest and comes at you from behind.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Give it no dark to hide in, she said, or nothing behind you to come from.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: It cannot bear being seen. Lola was right about that one.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Nothing behind me but rock, and nowhere for it to be. It gave up.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Gone. Lola would say it will be back for someone else, just not tonight.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: This is the same rock. Lola said the tikbalang walks you in circles until you give up.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: It lets its own kind through, she said. And it hates to lose a race.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: The same rock again. Whichever way I go, it brings me back.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: To the far side, then. All the way, and no stopping.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: It got there first. Back to the rock.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: It took me for one of its own, and stepped aside.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: It does not chase what it does not hunt. Lola said that was the trick.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Beat it. Lola said it never forgives that -- but it keeps its word.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Smoke, and somebody up there smoking it. Lola said the kapre sits high and keeps to itself, and the smoke turns you round.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Turned round in the smoke again. I am back where I came in.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: There it is. It was only sitting up there smoking, the whole time.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Down it comes, and off it goes. I did not have to be so hard on it.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Knocked clean out of its hand. It will not sit there smoking at anyone else tonight.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Somewhere to stop. Lola said the far side of the woods is the worst of it. Fill the lamp first.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Warm again. Whatever is past here, I will meet it with a full lamp.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: A baby crying, out here? Lola said: if you hear a child in the woods, you do not go to it. You stay on the path.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: That was never a baby. Lola said the light shows it for what it is, and it cannot stand to be seen.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I kept to the path, and it could not come to me. It is still crying back there.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: It cried like a child the whole time. Lola never told me what to do about that, and I wish she had.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Lola said the bungisngis laughs at everything, and that laughing is the only thing stronger than it is.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Only half of her is up there. Lola said: find where she left the rest of herself, and salt it.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Or keep her busy until morning. She cannot put herself back together in the **light**.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: This is the clearing in the painting. They are all coming, are they not.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Then I only have to last until morning.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Morning. Lola named every one of them for me, one by one. I needed every one.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: The woods again. Keep the lamp close.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Listen. Nothing yet.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Again. I know these woods better than they know me now.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Up the mountain from the sea. My clothes are still salty.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Good. Lola said they cannot stand salt.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Last time I mostly asked, and they mostly let me by.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Last time I mostly went round them. Quiet, and quick.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Last time I mostly fought my way through. I am not sure Lola would have.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Lola said the town at the foot of this mountain is called Los Baños, the baths, for the hot springs it keeps warm.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: People say Makiling has a keeper, Maria Makiling. Take from her forest without asking, they say, and you will not find the way down.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: From the lake, Lola said, the mountain looks like a woman lying on her back. That is where the story of its keeper comes from.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: The forest on Makiling is kept for learning now. People come up to put a name to everything that grows in it.

conversations.$comment: Played by LevelBase._run_conversation the first time she arrives. Steps point at hooks above.
